342653.title: Homogeneous block count conjecture for braid words
342653.review_depth: arXiv v2 (current) TeX read: homogeneous braids, Conjecture HBGR (Artin-Tits presentation of HBM(e)), Proposition (Murasugi), Lemma Inequalities, Theorem HomogeneousAreGeodesic, Remark (minimal diagrams keep the sign vector), Conjecture Wreathlike (line 389); web searches (no resolution; Alekseev 2024 Algebra i Analiz extends minimality to closed braids)
342653.summary: Weak form of the source's HBGR conjecture. Two remarks. (1) With at most two homogeneous blocks the claim already follows from the source: homogeneous words are geodesic, so the length P+N is invariant, and the exponent sum P-N is invariant. The first open case therefore has three blocks, e.g. e = (+,+,-,+). (2) The paraphrase is ambiguous when an index is absent from a word: the block numbering then depends on an arbitrary sign choice. That is a wording defect worth zero credit, not a counterexample. Exhaustive computation over all e-homogeneous words, with braids identified by the faithful Artin action on F_n: no braid has two words with different block counts, up to length 12 for ++-+ (543,100 braids at length 12) and +--+ (444,276), and up to length 11 for ++-++ (554,077). Moreover the number of distinct braids at each length equals the Saito growth series of the conjectured Artin-Tits monoid, so HBGR itself holds up to those lengths. A Burau-minor invariant route was tested and fails: on sigma2 sigma3^-1 sigma4^10 sigma3^-1 sigma2 sigma1 the 2x2 principal minor has max t-degree 11, while c_0 = 3. No proof, no counterexample.

343222.title: The planar graph positive-valued cover degeneracy conjecture
343222.review_depth: arXiv v4 (Discrete Math 2022) TeX read: definitions of cover, strictly f-degenerate transversal; Problem 4 conjecture (line 817) after Thomassen's theorems; web search (no resolution; Nakprasit partial for f in {0,1,2}; Li-Wang minor-free extensions)

A minimal counterexample needs min degree >= 5 (>= 12 vertices) together with a cover and an f-assignment, a search space far beyond capped Python without SAT (which this lane forbids). Disposed.

343238.title: Conjectural Brouwer inequality for Laplacian spectra of simplicial complexes
343238.review_depth: arXiv v1 (only version) TeX read: Conjecture red / Conjecture 3 (lines 86-91, 389-392), Laplacian L = d_{k-1} d_{k-1}^T (line 306), proofs for t = 1, 2 and the last partial sums; Abebe-Pfeffer 2012 REU report (Reiner REU site) read (three variants; SAGE found no counterexamples); Lew arXiv:2508.04209 TeX read (Theorem 1.3 thm:degree_bound, Corollary 1.4, Conjecture conj:higher_brouwer, Section conclusion); Kothari-Tudose arXiv:2606.12197 abstract (Brouwer's conjecture proved); Huang arXiv:2607.20051 and Zhang-Song-Fan arXiv:2607.20910 TeX read (Duval-Reiner counterexamples; Huang's seeds F16 and F15 have s_5 about 33+ while Abebe's bound is 67)
343238.summary: TRUE in full scope. k = 2 is Brouwer's conjecture, proved by Kothari-Tudose (2026). For k >= 3 (r = k-1 >= 2) it follows in about ten lines. Lew's Theorem 1.3 bounds s_t by the sum of the (r+1)t largest ridge degrees, which is at most r f_r + |F'|, where F' is the set of facets whose whole boundary lies in the chosen (r+1)t ridges. Lovasz's Kruskal-Katona theorem together with C(t+r, r) >= (r+1)t (valid for r >= 2) gives |F'| <= C(t+r, r+1). For (r+1)t > f_{r-1}, the trace bound plus the same Kruskal-Katona estimate applies. Lew does not state this consequence, and no source found does. It is a routine bridge from published and classical results, so zero credit is expected (outputs/343238-bridge-proof.md). Numerical diagnostic: random pure 2- and 3-complexes, maximum excess 0.
343238.credit_claim: none (routine bridge: Lew 2025 Thm 1.3 + Lovasz-Kruskal-Katona; k=2 is Kothari-Tudose 2026)

343468.title: Postnikov's 2-adic valuation conjecture for Morse link and Catalan numbers
343468.review_depth: arXiv v1 (Gao-Gu) TeX read: Section 4.4 Conjecture (Postnikov) and its generalisation to weights (2x+1)^{2k}; Postnikov "Counting Morse curves and links" (math.mit.edu brief) read: Conjecture 3.4 (alpha bits, records, d2(R_n) = s(n) + t_alpha(n-2) + 1) verified there for n <= 100,000 with the 2-adic integer pinned mod 2^20 (549719); RSI 2025 report (Pramatarova) and arXiv:2510.14956 abstract (periodicity only); web searches
343468.summary: Independent exact computation of L_n (weights (2h+1)^2) and v2(L_n - C_n) for 2 <= n <= 3500: consistent with v2(L_n - C_n) = s2(n) + v2(n - alpha) + 2, with alpha = 9047 mod 2^14 (binary 10001101010111; low six bits 010111 as stated) and record values matching Postnikov's (343, 855, 9047). Postnikov's own check reaches n <= 100,000, so no counterexample is reachable here. A proof needs new 2-adic theory beyond Postnikov-Sagan and Gao-Gu. Parked.

343505.title: Medvedoff–Morrison conjecture on generalised shuffle groups
343505.review_depth: arXiv v1 abstract read; Xia-Zhang-Zhang-Zhu, A complete classification of shuffle groups, arXiv:2304.01037 v4 = Forum Math. Sigma 12 (2024) e104: abstract and TeX read (Conjecture conk, line 234; Remark, line 238 on the parity determination; Theorem confirming all cases)
343505.summary: Known result. Xia-Zhang-Zhang-Zhu prove that G_{k,kn} contains A_{kn} for k >= 3, n not a power of k, and (k,n) != (4,2^f). Their Remark (after Medvedoff-Morrison Theorem 1) shows that G_{k,kn} <= A_{kn} exactly when n = 0 mod 4, or n = 2 mod 4 with k = 0,1 mod 4. This is precisely the Alt/Sym split in the MathDB statement, which is therefore fully proved (published 2024). Zero credit.

344494.title: The weaker mean subtree order conjecture for connected noncomplete graphs
344494.review_depth: arXiv v1 (JGT 2021) TeX read (Conjecture AddConjecture; computer search to order 8); Cambie-Chen-Hao-Tokar arXiv:2308.12808 abstract; Cambie-Jooken-Wagner arXiv:2508.20593 v2 (Sept 2026) TeX read: Conjecture conj:main2(b) still open, Theorem thr:strong_counterexamples (barbell D_{n,w}: only one edge class increases mu), commented exhaustive check n <= 10; GitHub JorikJooken/averageSubtreeOrderOfGraphs noted
344494.summary: The weaker Cameron-Mol conjecture is still open as of Sept 2026 (CJW v2 proves K_n is the maximum but leaves the edge-addition conjecture open). Exact tools: mu(G+uv) is obtained from ordered pairs of disjoint subtrees containing u and v respectively. They reproduce Cameron-Mol's K_{2,n-2} decrease from n = 8. Structured searches all found some increasing non-edge: barbells (w <= 5, n <= 12), closed-form K_{a,b} for a <= 14 and b <= 30 (the large-side edge always increases, delta about c/a), and complete multipartite graphs such as 2,3,9 / 2,4,8 / 3,4,12 / 2,6,6 / 1,1,6,6 (the largest part always increases). Asymptotic reasoning (CJW Case 4) shows that a P3 through a clique vertex in clique-dominated graphs always increases, so a counterexample must avoid dominant cliques. No counterexample, no proof.

344776.title: Brown–Erey's 2-connected graph coloring conjecture
344776.review_depth: arXiv v1 (SIAM DM 2021) TeX read (Theorem thm:2-conn at x = k; Conjecture conj:tomescu-2conn); Yang arXiv:2310.16382 TeX read (Brown-Erey conjecture with bound (x-1)_{k-1}((x-1)^{n-k+1}+(-1)^{n-k}); proved when omega = k or alpha = 2; "wide open")
344776.summary: The MathDB paraphrase writes (x)_k instead of (x-1)_{k-1}. That bound is x/(x-1) times weaker, and its equality clause is then literally false (G_{n,k} attains the smaller value). This is a paraphrase defect worth zero credit; we work from the source. Source conjecture: proved at x = k (EEFH), for omega = k or alpha = 2 (Yang), and for very large x (Brown-Erey). Analysis: attaching long ears to a core H reduces the comparison to Tomescu's general-x bound, proved for k = 4, 5 by Knox-Mohar, and cores with omega < k are denser. No promising finite counterexample route. Parked.

344926.title: Pasotti–Pellegrini's odd-order near-factor conjecture
344926.review_depth: arXiv v2 (current) TeX read: Meszka / Pasotti-Pellegrini conjecture (lines 160-176; prime case solved by Preissmann-Mischler); Pasotti-Pellegrini 2016 (arXiv:1404.3890) verified v <= 23 (per search abstract); web searches (no later extension)
344926.summary: Exact search with an exhaustive DFS (memoised, parity-pruned, MRV), with every found realisation re-verified. All boundary lists were realisable: v = 25, lists within 2 of the multiples-of-5 bound (9,240 lists); v = 27, within 1 of the bounds for 3 and 9 (24,957); v = 33, exactly at the bounds for 3 or 11 (54,264); v = 35, exactly at the bounds for 5 or 7 (24,480). An early timeout on v = 27 was an artefact of DFS ordering and was resolved by the improved solver. A refutation would in any case be a nonexistence certificate, expensive in Lean. This is near the parked 329760 Alspach sequencing family. Parked.
